name: RadioButton
description: One radio button — a real `<input type="radio">`, so the platform supplies the checked state, the shared-`name` grouping and form submission. A radio alone is not a pattern (APG's radio group is a set with one label and arrow keys — that is `RadioGroup`). It reads no context and calls no hook, which is what lets a Server Component render it with no client boundary.

props.name: name
props.description: The name the radios of one set share — it is what makes them one choice rather than several.

props.name: props
props.description: Attributes for the `<input>` itself. `type` is the component's.

props.name: onInput
props.description: Fires on every click or keystroke. On a radio this is the same moment as `onChange`.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Fires when this radio becomes the chosen one. A radio never fires it on being cleared.

props.name: value
props.description: What the set submits when this option is the chosen one.

props.name: autoFocus
props.description: Focus it on mount. One per page at most — a stolen focus is a lost place in the document.

props.name: readOnly
props.description: Rendered and read, but not selectable. Unlike `disabled` it stays in the tab order and submits.

props.name: defaultChecked
props.description: Makes this the chosen option to begin with, when the set is uncontrolled.

props.name: label
props.description: The text beside the radio, rendered inside a `<label>` that wraps the input.

props.name: labelProps
props.description: Styles for the wrapping `<label>`: the row's layout, not the radio's own appearance.

keyboard.action: Enters the set once, landing on the chosen option — or on the first, when none is chosen. Tab again leaves the set entirely.
The next or previous radio of the same `name`, choosing it as focus arrives, wrapping at both ends. The browser supplies this, so it works with no `RadioGroup`.

a11y: A real `<input type="radio">`, so the checked state, the roving tab stop across a `name` and form submission are the platform's rather than this component's.
`label` renders the `<label>` wrapping the input, which is what names this option. What names the *set* is a `RadioGroup`, or a `<fieldset>` with a legend of your own.
